note: Adversarial review findings (item-quality and compliance lenses) from the 15-17 Oct review round, recovered from the workflow transcripts after the device move. Not yet acted on.

compliance.verdict:
The mechanical checks pass. I re-ran ./gb tier-f gates (4 min 12 s): 10/10 solvability, 224 tokens, 3/3 variants reach V5, 9 valid mutants all killed. gates.json content is unchanged. build.py regenerated task.json, reference.grc and all 3 variants byte for byte (scratch copy in ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-03/regen). The canary GUID appears only in task.json. id, directory and split are consistent (test). The reference signature hashes to test. Licence, source, cluster_id, provenance, review, perturbation and level L1 fields follow the rules.

Fairness and compliance claims did not hold up. (1) HIGH: the instruction never says the flowgraph must run without limit or produce at least 65,536 samples. A correct answer that writes a finite file with a Head block (40,000 or 10,000 samples) fails V4 liveness. Sibling items carry an explicit 'keep running / do not limit the number of samples' sentence; this one does not. (2) MEDIUM: the stated cutoffs and transition width are not enforced. Width 1000/1250 and cutoff shifts of ±250 Hz pass V5, and the authored mutants are all large changes, so the 100 % kill rate overstates the oracle. (3) MEDIUM: the item is a template twin of dev item gbf-dev-02 (15 shared 8-grams, same chain and criteria); only the inert Throttle's position decides dev versus test. (4) MEDIUM: variant v3's own chain signature hashes to train, so training-side generators may produce functional twins. Lower-severity record issues: the seed requirement is unchecked yet listed in spec_properties, one mutation label is wrong, and the disjointness line omits the level check shared with t08.

Not ready for acceptance until F1 is fixed. F2 and F3 need a team decision. Task files untouched; scratch probes in C:\Users\Lenovo\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Lenovo-Documents--MScAC-2701-ml-ops-project-project\e3a3c780-e6be-4b4a-8abe-931944b53353\scratchpad\rev03\ (probe.py, edges.py).

findings.claim: The task needs an unbounded run, but the instruction never says so. A correct answer that limits the file with a Head block fails at V4. The observation needs 65,536 items (1.64 s at 40 kHz), more than most items need. The sentence 'so that every run writes the same samples' even suggests a fixed-length file.
findings.evidence: Scratch ladder probes (~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-03/probe.py) on reference.grc with a Head block inserted before the File Sink: Head 40000 (1 s of output) gives V4 'liveness: an observation point received too few items {'out': 40000}'. Head 10000 also fails V4. Head 100000 passes V5. task.json observation.run = {n_items: 65536, min_items: 65536}. Several sibling items say this explicitly: gbf-dev-01, gbf-dev-02 and gbf-test-02 ('do not limit the number of samples'), gbf-dev-03, gbf-test-04 and gbf-test-07 ('keep/run (continuously) until it is stopped'). gbf-test-03 has no such sentence. Eval plan §5.4 says everything needed to solve the task must be in the instruction.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the sentence gbf-dev-02 uses: 'The flowgraph should keep running until it is stopped; do not limit the number of samples.' Or state a minimum output length of at least 65,536 samples (e.g. 'at least 2 s / 80,000 samples'). Consider also dropping 'so that every run writes the same samples'. Then re-run the gates.

findings.claim: The instruction gives exact filter numbers (lower cutoff 6 kHz, upper cutoff 9 kHz, transition width 500 Hz), but the oracle only checks the looser acceptance criteria. Edits that break those numbers still pass V5. In effect the band edges have a tolerance of about ±250 Hz (about 4 %) and the transition width up to about 2.5×. The 9 authored mutants are all large changes, so the 100 % kill rate makes the oracle look stronger than it is.
findings.evidence: Scratch probes on reference.grc that still reach V5 (the RMS value P5 is in brackets): transition width 1000 (0.732) and 1250 (0.717); low_cutoff 6250 (0.717) and 5750 (0.784); high_cutoff 9250 (0.784) and 8750 (0.719). All also pass P2-P4. Adding just these 4 spec-breaking mutants gives 9/13 killed (69 %, below the 90 % gate). The authored mutants are x0.5, x1.25, 6.5 kHz, bypass, gain 2, amp 1, uniform noise, samp_rate 48k and wrong tap. Guidance says tolerances come from the spec, e.g. frequency ±1 %. A check is feasible: I computed |H|^2 with GR 3.10 firdes. Valid designs (Hamming, Hann, Blackman, Kaiser and rectangular windows; band_pass_2 at 60 dB; the HPF+LPF cascade; widths 200-500 Hz) put 0.033-0.055 of the power in each of 6.0-6.2 and 8.8-9.0 kHz, and ≤ 0.0004 in each of 5.5-5.8 and 9.2-9.5 kHz. For comparison: width 1000 puts 0.0023 in the outer bands, lo 6250 puts 0.0031 in 6.0-6.2, and lo 5750 puts 0.0109 in 5.5-5.8.
findings.suggested_fix: Choose one. (a) Make the acceptance criteria the whole spec: drop 'lower cutoff 6 kHz, upper cutoff 9 kHz, transition width 500 Hz' as separate requirements and keep only the power and RMS criteria. (b) Keep the numbers, state edge criteria in the instruction and check them. For example: each of 6.0-6.2 kHz and 8.8-9.0 kHz holds at least 2 % of the power, and each of 5.5-5.8 kHz and 9.2-9.5 kHz holds at most 0.1 %. Add near-miss mutants (width 1000, lo 6250, lo 5750, hi 9250) to the mutation list. Re-verify the variants and the 300-seed robustness.

findings.claim: gbf-test-03 is a template twin of the dev item gbf-dev-02. It passes the signature split only because an inert Throttle sits on the other side of the filter. Dev-02's chain order is a valid answer to this test item, and that order hashes to dev.
findings.evidence: gbf-dev-02 reference: analog_noise_source_x -> band_pass_filter (500 Hz transition, unity gain) -> blocks_throttle2 -> blocks_file_sink. Its acceptance criteria are 'at least 90 % of the power must lie between …, less than 1 % … above/below …, RMS level must be about … (within 5 %)'. The two instructions share 15 eight-word sequences, e.g. 'at least 90 % of the power must lie between' and 'unity gain in the passband. write the filtered signal as'. signature_split gives 'dev' for analog_noise_source_x|band_pass_filter|blocks_throttle2|blocks_file_sink, but 'test' for the same chain with the throttle before the filter and 'test' with no throttle. The throttle does nothing in the headless run. Eval plan §4.1: the dev split drives checkpoint selection and early stopping. §4.3: flowgraphs from one source stay in one split. gbf-dev-08 (float Gaussian noise band-passed to 6-18 kHz) is also thematically close.
findings.suggested_fix: Change test-03 substantively, e.g. a different family, a low-pass or high-pass noise shaping theme, or different acceptance features such as spectral-flatness quarters or a notch. Or move one of the pair so both twins share a split. Longer term, hash a canonical signature (drop blocks_throttle/throttle2, map filter and noise-source aliases) and assert that no dev/test pair shares one.

findings.claim: The item's own variant v3 has a chain signature that hashes to train, as do other valid solution chains. The signature rule therefore lets training-side generators emit functional twins of this test item, against compose.py's stated goal that a test chain is never a template twin of a training chain.
findings.evidence: signature_split: 'train' for analog_fastnoise_source_x|band_pass_filter|blocks_throttle2|blocks_file_sink (variant v3's exact chain), 'train' for analog_fastnoise_source_x|band_pass_filter|blocks_file_sink, and 'train' for analog_noise_source_x|blocks_throttle2|fft_filter_xxx|blocks_file_sink. Probe 'fft_filter' (reference with fft_filter_xxx and firdes taps) passes V5. build.py only asserts the reference's signature. The disjointness field says only 'its chain signature hashes to the test split'.
findings.suggested_fix: Record this item's functional signature in an exclusion list that training-side generators must respect (any noise source -> band-pass or HPF+LPF -> sink). Or canonicalise signatures before hashing (drop throttle, merge fastnoise with noise and the filter implementations). Mention the residual risk in the disjointness line.

findings.claim: The instruction requires the fixed seed 2718, but nothing checks it. spec_properties lists P7 (seed, explicitly not checked) and P8 (design, only indirect), although spec_properties is meant to list behaviours the instruction requires and the oracle checks. A model that ignores the seed gets full credit.
findings.evidence: Probe seed_0_default: V5 passes (RMS 0.7499). Probe seed_1: V5 passes. task.json spec_properties P7: 'not observable within a single run and therefore not checked'.
findings.suggested_fix: Either drop the seed sentence from the instruction and keep the seed only in the reference for gate determinism, or keep it and move P7/P8 out of spec_properties into review notes so the record matches what is checked.

findings.claim: Two record fields are inaccurate. Mutant 3's 'breaks' label is wrong. The disjointness line understates the overlap with t08.
findings.evidence: Mutant 3 (low_cutoff 6500) says 'P5 keeps 6-9 kHz (passband narrowed to 6.5-9 kHz)'. P5 is the RMS level property; the narrowed band is a P8/P2 design violation that only P5 detects. The disjointness line says the task 'is judged on where the output power lies', but P5 also checks that the level written to a file matches the theoretical value. That is the core of training-side t08_run_verify_probe ('noise source feeding a file … tell me if the measured level matches theory').
findings.suggested_fix: Relabel to e.g. 'P8 passband 6-9 kHz (narrowed to 6.5-9 kHz; detected via the P5 level)'. In the disjointness line, acknowledge the shared level-vs-theory element and name the band-pass filtering as the distinguishing core.

item-quality.verdict: Mostly sound, but not ready to accept as is. The build is solvable from the instruction alone. Every number the oracle uses is stated, the observation point is named unambiguously, and nothing leaks the solution. L1/build is correct (4 functional blocks, single-rate chain). The canary appears only in task.json. Valid alternatives I tried are accepted by ./gb ladder: Hann, Blackman, Kaiser, Blackman-Harris and band_pass_2 windows, an HPF+LPF cascade, a 100 Hz or 50 Hz transition, a full-path file name, and a rectangular window with seed 2718 on either noise source. Wrong cutoffs are rejected, including a passband-edge (optfir 6-9 kHz) design and shifts of 200 Hz or more, which the explicit RMS requirement justifies. Four findings survive. The most serious is a hidden requirement: the run needs 65536 samples, and a correct answer that writes a fixed 1 s file (Head of 40000) fails V4. Sibling items already fix this with the "keep running until it is stopped" sentence. Second, the stated 500 Hz transition width is only loosely enforced: 1000 Hz passes V5. Third, the seed is stated but cannot be checked. Fourth, the theme reaches other splits through trivially different chain signatures: variant v3's chain hashes to train, and gbf-dev-02 is a dev template twin. Fixing F1 and F2 and re-running the gates should make the item acceptable. Scratch answers are in ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-03 and C:\Users\Lenovo\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Lenovo-Documents--MScAC-2701-ml-ops-project-project\e3a3c780-e6be-4b4a-8abe-931944b53353\scratchpad\gbf-test-03-review (sim.py, resp.py, *.grc).

findings.claim: The oracle needs at least 65536 samples (1.64 s at 40 kHz) at bandnoise.dat, but the instruction never says the flowgraph must keep running or must not limit the number of samples. A correct answer that writes a fixed-length file is rejected at V4. The instruction's own wording, "fixed seed 2718 so that every run writes the same samples", invites a fixed-length file.
findings.evidence: Scratch answer ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-03/a_head_1s.grc (copy in scratchpad gbf-test-03-review/): it is the reference design (Noise Source float, amp 2.0, seed 2718 -> Band Pass Filter 6000/9000/500 Hamming -> File Sink bandnoise.dat) with a Head block of int(samp_rate) = 40000 items (1 s) before the sink. ./gb ladder with this task.json gives highest_passed V3, first_failed V4: "liveness: an observation point received too few items {'out': 40000}" (finished_on_its_own True). task.json observation.run sets n_items = min_items = 65536, and no spec_property covers it. Six sibling items (gbf-dev-01, gbf-dev-02, gbf-dev-03, gbf-test-02, gbf-test-04, gbf-test-07) state "The flowgraph should keep running until it is stopped; do not limit the number of samples". gbf-dev-02 also lists it as spec property P8 ("checked at V4 (liveness needs 65536 items ...)"). gbf-test-03 has neither.
findings.suggested_fix: Append "The flowgraph should keep running until it is stopped; do not limit the number of samples." to the instruction. Add a spec property such as "P9 runs until stopped: checked at V4 (liveness needs 65536 items at the File Sink; a graph that stops itself earlier fails V4)". Consider rewording "so that every run writes the same samples" to "so that the noise is reproducible", since an unbounded file is not the same length on every run.

findings.claim: The instruction requires a 500 Hz transition width, and that width is measurable, but the oracle accepts a design with twice that width. The stopband edges at 5 kHz and 10 kHz lie 1 kHz from the cutoffs, and the RMS tolerance is wide enough, so any width up to about 1 kHz passes. No mutant changes the width, so the mutation gate did not reveal this.
findings.evidence: Scratch answer b_width1000_fullpath.grc (reference with width '1000') passes V5 in ./gb ladder: in-band 0.9753, below 5 kHz 3.9e-5, above 10 kHz 5.3e-5, RMS 0.7318 (limits 0.7125-0.7875). Simulating the same filter with GNU Radio blocks over seeds 1-40: width 1500 passes 8/40 and width 2000 passes 0/40, so the oracle's real limit is roughly 'width at most about 1 kHz'. Noise-free power fractions computed with GNU Radio's filter-design functions, per side, in 5.5-5.75 kHz and 9.25-9.5 kHz: 500 Hz designs give Hamming 1.3e-5, Hann 1.2e-4, Blackman 8e-6, Kaiser 2.5e-6, band_pass_2 2.2e-6, HPF+LPF cascade 1.3e-5, rectangular 2.4e-4. 1000 Hz designs give Hamming 1.3e-3, Blackman 1.0e-3, Hann 3.0e-3. A check can therefore tell 500 Hz from 1000 Hz without rejecting any window choice.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) add two band_fraction checks, [5500, 5750] Hz and [9250, 9500] Hz, each max 5e-4, state them in the instruction (e.g. "less than 0.05 % of the power may lie between 5.5 and 5.75 kHz, and likewise between 9.25 and 9.5 kHz"), add a width x2 mutant (scale_param width 2.0) and re-run the gates. Or (b) reword the instruction so the stated number matches what is checked, e.g. "transition width 500 Hz (at most 1 kHz)", and add the width x2 case to the spec_properties note.

findings.claim: The instruction requires the fixed seed 2718, but the oracle cannot check it, so any seed (including the default 0) passes. The model is given a requirement with no consequence. The stated reason ("so that every run writes the same samples") is a promise an unbounded File Sink cannot keep, and it pushes toward the fixed-length file problem in F1.
findings.evidence: spec_properties P7: "fixed seed 2718: not observable within a single run and therefore not checked". The reference passes 40/40 random seeds in simulation. Scratch answer c_rect_seed0.grc (seed '0') passes V5. An exact-sequence check would wrongly reject variant v3 (Fast Noise Source with seed 2718 produces a different sequence), so the seed cannot be checked fairly across noise blocks. Sibling gbf-dev-02 avoids this by asking for no seed (its P10).
findings.suggested_fix: If the slot brief's "fixed seed" must stay, keep it but drop the clause "so that every run writes the same samples" (or replace it with "for reproducibility"), and leave P7 as it is. Otherwise remove the seed from the instruction and keep it only in the reference, as gbf-dev-02 does.

findings.claim: The band-limited-noise theme is not confined to the test split. One of this item's own accepted solutions (variant v3) has a chain signature that hashes to train. Dev item gbf-dev-02 uses the same chain blocks (throttle moved) and the same task template. compose.py intends the signature partition to ensure "a test chain is never a template twin of a training chain", but swapping or reordering one block defeats it.
findings.evidence: compose.signature_split results: analog_noise_source_x|blocks_throttle2|band_pass_filter|blocks_file_sink (this reference) = test. analog_fastnoise_source_x|band_pass_filter|blocks_throttle2|blocks_file_sink (variant v3's exact chain) = train. analog_fastnoise_source_x|band_pass_filter|blocks_file_sink = train. analog_noise_source_x|band_pass_filter|blocks_throttle2|blocks_file_sink (gbf-dev-02 cluster_id) = dev. gbf-dev-02 builds band-pass-filtered Gaussian noise with a 500 Hz transition and unity gain, using the same acceptance template (at least 90 % in band, less than 1 % outside, RMS within 5 %, 65536-item run). The disjointness field does not mention either overlap. No training-side chain generator exists in the repo yet, so the training risk is latent.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalise chain signatures before hashing: drop throttles, map analog_fastnoise_source_x to analog_noise_source_x, and treat HPF+LPF or fir_filter_xxx with firdes.band_pass taps as band_pass_filter. Alternatively, give training-side generators a deny-list of test themes (e.g. band-limited noise via band-pass). Record the gbf-dev-02 overlap in disjointness, or re-theme one of the two items.
